signals.title: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets
signals.content: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simple and transparent to run, and do not require central knowledge of private capabilities and costs. However, FPAs are not truthful: participants may bid less than their true value in the hope of a larger profit, and the prompt may then be allocated to someone other than the bidder who values it the most. This welfare loss is quantified by the $\textit{price-of-anarchy}$ (PoA). In this paper, we argue that agentic markets are likely to possess features that reduce the price-of-anarchy. The first is a $\textit{competitive floor}$, which occurs when multiple bidders usually value the prompt above some baseline share of the optimal welfare (e.g., because the best models are often distilled into cheaper alternatives, which perform similarly). We show that competition among them then limits the welfare loss, which can be driven to zero as the floor rises. The second feature is $\textit{near-independence}$ of values after conditioning on the prompt, which occurs when most of the predictable variation in the expected value is determined by the difficulty of the prompt. As the value distribution approaches conditional independence, we can derive an efficiency guarantee that approaches a factor of $1 - 1/e^2$ of the optimal welfare. Thus, both features give rise to welfare lower bounds that are significantly better than the well-known general case of $1 - 1/e$. We validate these results empirically using auctions with strategic bidders simulated on the EmbedLLM prompt routing dataset.

signals.brief_en:
Title: Price of Anarchy of First‑Price Auctions in Agentic Markets

An agentic market is a decentralized serving‑time environment where AI agents bid for each user prompt. An agent’s bid reflects its expected net value (reward minus inference cost). First‑price auctions (FPAs) allocate prompts by awarding them to the highest bidder, who pays its own bid. FPAs are simple and require no central knowledge of private costs, but they are not strategy‑proof: bidders may shade their bids, potentially assigning the prompt to a lower‑valued agent. The resulting welfare loss is measured by the price‑of‑anarchy (PoA).

Two market features are likely to curb PoA:
1. **Competitive floor** – many agents typically value a prompt above a baseline share of optimal welfare (e.g., because top‑tier models are often distilled into cheaper, similarly performing variants). This competition raises the minimum bid and can drive PoA toward zero as the floor rises.
2. **Near‑independence of values** – after conditioning on the prompt, agents’ values are largely independent because most predictable variation stems from prompt difficulty rather than model specifics. This reduces strategic interdependence and further limits welfare loss.

These observations suggest that, despite the inherent inefficiency of FPAs, agentic markets may exhibit low PoA under realistic conditions.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: تكلفة الفوضى في المزادات ذات السعر الأول في الأسواق الوكيلة

السوق الوكيلة هو بيئة لامركزية لتقديم الخدمات حيث تتنافس وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي على كل طلب مستخدم. يعكس عرض الوكيل القيمة المتوقعة الصافية (المكافأة مطروحًا منها تكلفة الاستدلال). تُخصص الطلبات في المزادات ذات السعر الأول (FPA) للمتقدم الأعلى، الذي يدفع عرضه. تُعد هذه الآلية بسيطة ولا تحتاج إلى معرفة مركزية لتكاليف الوكلاء الخاصة، لكنها غير صادقة استراتيجيًا: قد يخفض المتقدمون عروضهم، مما قد يُعطي الطلب لوكيل أقل قيمة. يُقاس فقدان الرفاهية الناتج بـ«تكلفة الفوضى» (PoA).

هناك ميزتان في السوق قد تقللان من PoA:
1. **الحد الأدنى التنافسي** – عادةً ما يقدّر عدة وكلاء الطلب بأكثر من حصة أساسية من الرفاهية المثلى (مثلاً لأن النماذج المتقدمة تُستخلص إلى نماذج أرخص ذات أداء مماثل). هذا التنافس يرفع الحد الأدنى للعرض ويمكن أن يدفع PoA نحو الصفر مع ارتفاع الحد.
2. **قرب الاستقلالية في القيم** – بعد شرط الطلب، تكون قيم الوكلاء مستقلة إلى حد كبير لأن معظم التباين القابل للتنبؤ يُحدده صعوبة الطلب وليس خصائص النموذج. يقلل هذا من التداخل الاستراتيجي ويحد من فقدان الرفاهية.

تشير هذه الملاحظات إلى أن المزادات ذات السعر الأول قد تُظهر PoA منخفضًا في الأسواق الوكيلة تحت ظروف واقعية، رغم عدم كفاءتها الجوهرية.

signals.title: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers
signals.content: Evaluations of classifiers (AI or human or agents) often assume a batch setting in which every agent produces labels on every example in a test set, which can be expensive or impractical in many contexts. This motivates online policies that adaptively select agents to query as examples arrive and update policies as outcomes are observed. We study the problem of selecting, in an online stream, the agent that best balances (i) predictive performance and (ii) subgroup fairness of a sensitive attribute, and that allows for delayed observations of true class labels. We formulate this as a Bayesian multi-armed bandit problem using Thompson Sampling, explicitly balancing accuracy and fairness. We conduct empirical evaluations on real-world datasets spanning problems involving tabular classifiers, large language models, and human labelers, demonstrating substantial reductions in regret relative to baselines. Our theoretical contributions include guarantees on the performance of the selected agent that incorporate both the accuracy and fairness aspects of the problem.

signals.brief_en:
Title: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers

This brief outlines recent work on online selection of classifiers that jointly optimizes predictive performance and subgroup fairness. Traditional evaluations assume a batch setting where every agent labels every example, which is often infeasible. The proposed approach treats the problem as a Bayesian multi‑armed bandit and applies Thompson Sampling to balance accuracy against fairness for a sensitive attribute, while handling delayed true‑label feedback. Empirical tests on diverse real‑world datasets—including tabular models, large language models, and human annotators—show significant regret reductions compared with standard baselines. Theoretical analysis provides performance guarantees that explicitly incorporate both accuracy and fairness criteria.

signals.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
signals.content: Understanding the social intelligence of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly important for applications involving human-AI interaction and multi-agent environments. Social intelligence comprises two aspects: cognitive intelligence, the ability to infer others' mental states, and behavioral intelligence, the ability to select appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals. Persuasion provides a natural testbed in which both aspects are simultaneously at play, yet prior benchmarks typically evaluate them in isolation using synthetic scenarios. We introduce PerSo, a benchmark that evaluates both aspects on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView community, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct the evaluation tasks, validated through human annotation. Our evaluation of diverse LLMs shows that performance generally scales with model size but varies across dimensions. The strongest LLM slightly surpasses the best observed human performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant remains ahead on the cognitive task.

signals.brief_en:
Title: PerSo – Assessing LLM Social Intelligence in Real‑World Persuasion
Summary: PerSo is a new benchmark that measures two core components of social intelligence in large language models—cognitive (inferring others' mental states) and behavioral (choosing socially effective actions). It uses authentic persuasion dialogues from Reddit’s ChangeMyView community, generated via an LLM‑in‑the‑loop pipeline and validated by human annotators. Evaluation of multiple LLMs shows size‑related performance gains, but results differ by task: the top LLM slightly exceeds the best human score on the behavioral dimension, while humans still lead on the cognitive dimension. The benchmark highlights the need for integrated, real‑world testing of AI social capabilities.

العنوان: PerSo – تقييم الذكاء الاجتماعي للنماذج اللغوية الكبيرة في سيناريوهات الإقناع الواقعية
الملخص: يقدم PerSo معيارًا جديدًا يقيس مكوّنين أساسيين للذكاء الاجتماعي في النماذج اللغوية الكبيرة – الذكاء المعرفي (القدرة على استنتاج حالات العقل لدى الآخرين) والذكاء السلوكي (اختيار الأفعال الاجتماعية المناسبة لتحقيق أهداف). يعتمد على حوارات إقناع حقيقية من مجتمع Reddit ChangeMyView، تُنشأ عبر خط أنابيب يدمج نموذجًا لغويًا وتُصادق عليها تعليقات بشرية. أظهرت التقييمات أن الأداء يزداد مع حجم النموذج، لكن الفروق تبقى بين البعدين: النموذج الأقوى يتفوق قليلاً على أفضل أداء بشري في المهمة السلوكية، بينما يظل الإنسان المتفوق في المهمة المعرفية. يبرز المعيار الحاجة إلى اختبارات متكاملة وواقعية لقدرات الذكاء الاجتماعي للذكاء الاصطناعي.

signals.title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
signals.content: 3D object composition is pivotal to digital content creation and robot simulation, while also serving as a critical testbed for physical intelligence in foundation models. Previous methods either leverage large language models to directly predict object coordinates, or utilize generative diffusion priors to synthesize composite images for visual alignment, both of which rely on static priors in digital spaces. However, these methods consistently struggle with complex compositions such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling and hidden containment, as these tasks require interactive construction processes involving global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation. To address these challenges, we propose PhySGA, a Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for 3D composition via agent exploration and physical simulation, enabling the universal interactive assembly of rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Directly applying vanilla LLMs or VLMs to this task proves insufficient, as current models inherently lack grounded physical understanding and interactive construction experience. To overcome this limitation, we design a collaborative feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent focuses on geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, while a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics for simulator state diagnosis and fine-grained closed-loop correction. Furthermore, Action Routers map semantic planning and analysis onto executable physical primitives within the simulator, while a task-specific Self-Evolving Skill Library distills historical trial-and-error feedback into reusable experiences, boosting success rates and minimizing exploration attempts. Extensive experiments within Isaac Sim demonstrate that PhySGA significantly surpasses existing methods in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.
signals.score_reason: academic/research signal; agentic AI relevance; retrieval/RAG relevance; large language model relevance. Final score: 56. Freshness: source age 0.92d.
signals.brief_en: PhySGA is a physics‑space grounded agentic framework that enables interactive 3D composition of rigid, articulated and deformable objects. It combines an Assembly Agent for global geometric planning with a Critic Agent that monitors contact dynamics and provides closed‑loop corrections via simulation. The system addresses limitations of LLM‑only or diffusion‑based approaches, which struggle with tasks requiring precise hanging, gravity‑driven settling, or hidden containment. By integrating feed‑forward planning and feedback from a physics simulator, PhySGA offers a more reliable, generalizable solution for digital content creation and robot simulation, though its performance still depends on the fidelity of the underlying simulator and the quality of the agent’s learned policies.
signals.brief_ar: PhySGA هو إطار عمل وكيل متمركز في الفضاء الفيزيائي يتيح تركيبًا تفاعليًا ثلاثي الأبعاد للأجسام الصلبة والمفصلية والقابلة للتشوه. يجمع بين وكيل تجميع يخطط هندسيًا على المستوى العالمي ووكيل ناقد يراقب ديناميكيات الاتصال ويقدم تصحيحات حلقة مغلقة عبر المحاكاة. يعالج هذا النظام قيود الأساليب التي تعتمد على نماذج اللغة الكبيرة أو الانتشار، والتي تواجه صعوبات في مهام التعليق الدقيق، والاستقرار تحت تأثير الجاذبية، أو الاحتواء المخفي. من خلال دمج التخطيط المسبق مع التغذية الراجعة من محاكي الفيزياء، يوفر PhySGA حلاً أكثر موثوقية وقابلية للتعميم لإنشاء المحتوى الرقمي ومحاكاة الروبوتات، مع بقاء الأداء مرتبطًا بدقة المحاكي وجودة سياسات الوكيل.

signals.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
signals.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions. However, this open-ended interface exposes a new vulnerability surface: an inattentive driver may issue instructions that are unsafe given the current scene, and a malicious user may issue dangerous ones on purpose. We present the first benchmark suite that evaluates navigation following and conflict awareness together, along with adversarial robustness. Existing VLAs fall short on both: SimLingo completes no language-instructed lane change in closed loop, and all models degrade sharply under conflicting signals. We propose SafeDriveVLA, the first driving VLA that (1) explicitly predicts a three-level navigation-compliance mode to decouple conflict reasoning from action generation, and (2) uses navigation-conditioned world model dreaming to inform this prediction. Unlike prior world models that roll out expert or planned actions, ours dreams of strictly following the navigation signal, showing when following is safe. SafeDriveVLA reaches 88.16 Driving Score (DS) and 68.64% Success Rate (SR) on Bench2Drive, lifts closed-loop language following by 49.3% and reduces collisions under unsafe instructions from 60 to 38 compared to the best SimLingo variant. Video demonstrations are available on our project page.

signals.brief_en: SafeDriveVLA introduces a navigation‑conditioned world‑model that predicts a three‑level compliance mode, separating conflict reasoning from action generation. This enables the system to "dream" outcomes of strictly following a natural‑language instruction and reject unsafe commands. In the Bench2Drive benchmark, SafeDriveVLA achieves an 88.16 driving score and 68.64% success rate, improves closed‑loop language following by 49.3% over SimLingo, and cuts collisions from unsafe instructions from 60 to 38. The work provides the first benchmark that jointly evaluates navigation compliance, conflict awareness, and adversarial robustness for vision‑language‑action autonomous driving models.
signals.brief_ar: يقدِّم SafeDriveVLA نموذجًا عالميًا مشروطًا بالملاحة يتنبأ بوضعية امتثال ثلاثية المستويات، مما يفصل بين استدلال الصراع وتوليد الإجراءات. يتيح ذلك للنظام "تخيل" نتائج الالتزام الصارم بتعليمات اللغة الطبيعية ورفض الأوامر غير الآمنة. في معيار Bench2Drive، يحقق SafeDriveVLA درجة قيادة 88.16٪ ومعدل نجاح 68.64٪، ويحسّن متابعة اللغة في الحلقة المغلقة بنسبة 49.3٪ مقارنةً بـ SimLingo، ويقلل التصادمات الناتجة عن التعليمات غير الآمنة من 60 إلى 38. يُعد هذا العمل أول معيار يقيم معًا الامتثال للملاحة، والوعي بالصراع، والصلابة ضد الهجمات للأنظمة ذات الرؤية‑اللغة‑الإجراء في القيادة الذاتية.

signals.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
signals.content: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average $3.16\times$ decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.

signals.brief_en: ReaDy introduces a speculative decoding technique that taps into the recurrent states of Hybrid Linear Attention (HLA) models to provide position‑specific context during token drafting. Each draft position uses a learned query to read supplementary information from the model's compact, accumulated state, which is merged into the draft representation via a lightweight residual update. Low‑rank reads and fused operators keep extra compute and I/O minimal. Integrated with DSpark’s parallel backbone and sequential head, ReaDy follows a two‑stage adaptation (reader capacity, state source, residual placement) validated by ablations. Across seven benchmarks (math, code, dialogue) on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU, ReaDy yields a 3.16× speedup over standard autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8‑27B, surpasses DSpark by 7.97% in throughput and 8.50% in accepted length, while preserving generation quality.
signals.brief_ar: يقدِّم ReaDy تقنية فك الترميز التخميني التي تستغل الحالات المتكررة لنماذج الانتباه الخطي الهجين (HLA) لتوفير سياق مخصص لكل موضع أثناء صياغة الرموز. يستخدم كل موضع استعلامًا مُتعلمًا لقراءة معلومات إضافية من الحالة المتراكمة للنموذج، ثم يُدمج هذا السياق في تمثيل الصياغة عبر تحديث متبقي خفيف الوزن. تُحافظ القراءات منخفضة الرتبة والعمليات المدمجة على الحد الأدنى من الحسابات والـ I/O. يُدمج ReaDy مع العمود الفقري المتوازي DSpark والرأس التتابعي، ويتبع استراتيجية تعديل من مرحلتين (سعة القارئ، مصدر الحالة، موضع المتبقي) تم اختبارها عبر تجارب إلغاء. على سبعة معايير تشمل الرياضيات، البرمجة، والحوار، وعلى وحدة معالجة رسومية NVIDIA B200 واحدة، يحقق ReaDy تسريعًا بمقدار 3.16× مقارنةً بالفك التلقائي التقليدي باستخدام Qwen3.8‑27B، ويتفوق على DSpark بزيادة 7.97% في الإنتاجية و8.50% في طول القبول، مع الحفاظ على جودة النص.
